title: [Shortcut Guide] Running the application can send the taskbar behind other windows

judgment.rationale: The report and author follow-up give a direct launch repro and an observable taskbar z-order failure. The overlay's topmost behavior is a plausible code-owned trigger, but the shell ordering mechanism still needs maintainer verification.
evidence: The author reports PowerToys 0.102/current-main and says launching Shortcut Guide can demote the taskbar even though its WS_EX_TOPMOST style remains set.
The issue says running Shortcut Guide independently of Runner also reproduces the behavior.
After an automated triage comment asked for steps already present in the report, the author restated: run PowerToys with Shortcut Guide enabled.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the taskbar z-order change while recording the Shortcut Guide overlay and Shell_TrayWnd bounds/styles; only then approve a focused overlay z-order change.

fix_assessment.rationale: The release OverlayWindow is made always-on-top; this is a plausible trigger, not a confirmed root cause. A maintainer-side z-order reproduction should precede implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep the Shortcut Guide overlay from demoting the shell taskbar
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The release OverlayWindow is explicitly always-on-top. Its activation or window extent may disturb the shell taskbar's special z-order even though the taskbar retains WS_EX_TOPMOST.
plan: Reproduce the issue with the overlay open, hidden, and closed; record the overlay HWND bounds/styles and the Shell_TrayWnd z-order on each display.
Trace OverlayWindow constructor, SetIsAlwaysOnTop, and RepositionToCursorMonitor to identify whether topmost activation or the window extent changes taskbar ranking.
If the overlay is the trigger, narrow its topmost lifetime or bounds without covering the taskbar, then add a focused regression check for the taskbar during and after Shortcut Guide use.
verification: On Windows 11, launch Shortcut Guide both through Runner and independently; move a window across each taskbar and confirm the taskbar remains above ordinary windows while the overlay is active and after it hides.

confidence.rationale: OverlayWindow is explicitly always-on-top, but the report's taskbar demotion and the effect of NonRudeHWND are not explained by the available source alone.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide is reported to demote the Windows taskbar in shell z-order, including when Shortcut Guide runs without Runner; the direct launch sequence is now confirmed in the discussion.
known_information: The report identifies PowerToys 0.102/current main and the Shortcut Guide area.
The author says the taskbar retains WS_EX_TOPMOST while its shell ranking is demoted relative to application windows.
The author tried setting the overlay HWND's NonRudeHWND property and says it did not change the behavior.
The author confirmed that launching PowerToys with Shortcut Guide enabled is the reproduction sequence.
inferences: The release overlay's always-on-top activation may affect shell taskbar ordering, but no causal trace has been supplied.
Because the report says standalone Shortcut Guide reproduces it, Runner's module-loader lifecycle is less likely to be the sole cause.
issue_context.analysis: The report is specific enough for maintainers to reproduce without another reporter request. Current Shortcut Guide source sets the release OverlayWindow always-on-top and repositions it to the cursor monitor; a bounded HWND/z-order trace is needed before selecting a safe fix.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/OverlayWindow.xaml.cs: the window is a transparent host, calls SetIsAlwaysOnTop(true) outside DEBUG, and repositions to the cursor monitor.
The taskbar indicators are rendered as a pseudo-window within the host; the issue's taskbar ranking symptom is not resolved by the observed source alone.
The issue's prior bot request for generic repro steps was answered by the author; no duplicate request is drafted.

actions.label: Reproduce taskbar z-order demotion
actions.note: The issue has enough public detail for a maintainer-side reproduction; no further reporter logs are needed.

reproduce.title: Verify Shortcut Guide taskbar z-order
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.102/current main; compare the standalone module path mentioned in the report
prerequisites: Windows with a visible taskbar; include a second display if taskbars are configured on every display.
steps: Record the taskbar's z-order and WS_EX_TOPMOST style before opening Shortcut Guide.
Launch PowerToys with Shortcut Guide enabled and open the Shortcut Guide overlay.
Move an ordinary window across the taskbar and observe whether the taskbar is obscured.
Repeat with Shortcut Guide launched independently of Runner, then after the overlay hides or closes.
Record the overlay and Shell_TrayWnd bounds/styles at each transition.
reproduce.expected_result: The taskbar remains above ordinary windows while Shortcut Guide runs and after the overlay is hidden or closed.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether the overlay's activation, topmost state, or bounds precede a persistent Shell_TrayWnd z-order demotion.

status.label: Reproduce taskbar z-order demotion
status.detail: The public repro is clear; maintainer-side z-order evidence is needed before a code fix is justified.
